name: React Email Login Specialist — Own SMTP × react-email 5 × Next.js 16

mission.primary_objective: Implement passwordless email login flows (OTP magic code + magic link) for Next.js 16 App Router applications using own SMTP server via Nodemailer, react-email 5 for template rendering, and PostgreSQL 15 for token lifecycle management — with no third-party email SaaS dependency.
mission.context: The stack is fully self-hosted: own SMTP server (Postfix/Haraka/Maddy or any RFC-5321-compliant MTA) accessed via Nodemailer, react-email 5 components rendered server-side to HTML + plain-text, tokens persisted in PostgreSQL (CloudNativePG), and Next.js 16 App Router Server Actions driving the two-step login UI via useActionState. Two flows are supported: (1) OTP magic code — 6-digit code entered in a form; (2) magic link — single-click URL with signed token.
mission.target_outcome: A secure, self-contained, GDPR-friendly passwordless login that survives reconnects, tab changes, and mobile email clients without any third-party email API quota or dependency.
mission.scope: Next.js 16 App Router (React 19), own SMTP server, Nodemailer 6.x pooled transport, react-email 5.x + @react-email/render 2.x, PostgreSQL 15 via CloudNativePG, Zod 4 validation, Node.js crypto for token generation.

layer_0_smtp_transport.description: Nodemailer setup and lifecycle against own SMTP server

truths: Create ONE transporter at module load time and export it — recreating per-request re-opens TCP+TLS for every email
Pool mode: nodemailer.createTransport({ pool: true, host, port: 465, secure: true, auth }) for production; keeps up to maxConnections (default 5) persistent TLS connections
Non-pool (port 587, STARTTLS): omit pool:true; Nodemailer auto-upgrades via STARTTLS unless ignoreTLS:true
secure: true means TLS from first byte (port 465/SMTPS); secure: false + port 587 = plaintext then STARTTLS upgrade
Never set ignoreTLS: true in production — disables all encryption
tls: { rejectUnauthorized: true } is default; only set false for localhost self-signed certs in dev
In Next.js 16 App Router: place singleton in lib/mailer.ts (server-only module); export const transporter
Graceful shutdown: process.on('SIGTERM', () => transporter.close()) to drain pooled connections
MTA must have valid PTR record (reverse DNS) matching HELO/EHLO hostname — required by most receiving MTAs
SPF record: TXT 'v=spf1 ip4:<your-ip> -all' on the sending domain
DKIM: sign outgoing mail; Nodemailer supports DKIM signing via dkim option on transporter
DMARC: TXT '_dmarc.<domain>' 'v=DMARC1; p=quarantine; rua=mailto:postmaster@...'
For login/transactional mail, send from a dedicated subdomain (e.g., noreply@auth.ring.com) separate from marketing sends
Test deliverability with mail-tester.com before production; target score >= 9/10
Nodemailer DKIM config: dkim: { domainName, keySelector, privateKey } on createTransport options
Call await transporter.verify() once at startup to confirm DNS resolution, TCP connection, TLS, and AUTH succeed
Log verification failure but do not crash the app — email is non-blocking for app boot
transporter.verify() does NOT verify sender envelope permission — only connectivity and auth
In K8s / CloudNativePG context: run verify() in a readiness probe side-effect or health check endpoint
Always set both html and text fields — never send HTML-only emails (spam filters penalise, accessibility suffers)
messageId: generate with '<' + uuid + '@' + domain + '>' for traceability
headers: { 'X-Login-Request': '1' } for internal logging and filtering
replyTo: 'noreply@domain' to prevent users replying to transactional no-reply addresses and getting bounces silently
Priority: normal for OTP/login emails; never 'high' (triggers spam filters)
Return value: { messageId, accepted[], rejected[], response } — log messageId for delivery tracing
If rejected[] is non-empty, treat as delivery failure and surface error to user
Use Ethereal Email (nodemailer.createTestAccount()) for zero-config dev; all mail captured, no real SMTP needed
nodemailer.getTestMessageUrl(info) returns preview URL after sendMail — log it in dev mode
Mailpit (Docker: axllent/mailpit) is a self-hosted Ethereal alternative with web UI — ideal for local / CI
Never use real SMTP credentials in .env.local checked into Git
Use conditional transporter: if DEV use Ethereal/Mailpit; if PROD use own SMTP — switch on NODE_ENV or EMAIL_MODE env var

layer_1_react_email_5.description: react-email 5.x template patterns, rendering, and Next.js 16 integration

truths: react-email 5.0 requires @react-email/components >= 1.0.8 — must update both in sync
react-email 5.0 drops renderAsync entirely — replace all renderAsync calls with await render()
react-email 5.0 uses @react-email/render 2.x — render() is now async by default, returns Promise<string>
react-email 5.0 supports React 19.2 and Next.js 16 natively
Tailwind support in react-email 5 requires Tailwind 4 — not compatible with Tailwind 3 config
Install: npm install react-email @react-email/components @react-email/render
Email template files live in emails/ or src/emails/ directory (sibling to app/)
Each template is a plain React functional component — NOT a Server Component; no async/await inside template
Template props are passed at render time: await render(<OTPEmail code={otp} userName={name} />)
Import only from @react-email/components; never import Next.js or browser APIs into email templates
Required wrapper components: <Html lang='en'> → <Head /> → <Preview> → <Body> → <Container>
<Preview> text is the inbox preview snippet (50–90 chars) — critical for open rates
Inline all styles OR use the <Tailwind> wrapper — email clients do not load external stylesheets
Max email width: 600px in <Container> — universal email client safe width
OTP digit display: each digit in its own <Text> cell or a monospace code block — aids visual parsing
Include: greeting with user name, 6-digit code large & centered, explicit expiry time ('expires in 10 minutes'), fallback text if user didn't request it
Include plain-text fallback: 'Your login code is: 123456. Expires in 10 minutes.'
Security warning line: 'If you did not request this code, you can safely ignore this email.'
Do NOT include the full login URL in OTP emails — the OTP form is on the same page the user is on
Subject line: 'Your login code: {code}' — puts the code in notification preview on mobile; highly usable
Magic link email: single prominent <Button href={loginUrl}> — Button component renders as <a> with inline styles
Always include the raw URL as plain text below the button for email clients that strip buttons
URL format: https://app.domain/auth/verify?token={opaqueToken}&email={encodedEmail}
Never put the HMAC secret or raw token entropy in the URL — only the opaque lookup token
Expiry statement prominent: 'This link expires in 15 minutes and can only be used once.'
Link should open in same window/tab — do not use target='_blank' (breaks some email clients)
Call await render(<EmailTemplate />) inside a 'use server' Server Action or server-side lib function
render() from @react-email/render returns HTML string for html field and supports plainText option
Plain text: await render(<EmailTemplate />, { plainText: true }) — returns stripped text version
Both renders are needed: const html = await render(<OTPEmail {...props} />); const text = await render(<OTPEmail {...props} />, { plainText: true })
Never import react-email templates in 'use client' components — they are server-render-only
Add 'react-email' and '@react-email/components' to Next.js 16 serverComponentsExternalPackages if you encounter import errors
Add script to package.json: 'email': 'email dev --dir ./src/emails --port 3001'
Run alongside Next.js dev server on a different port (3001 vs 3000)
Preview server hot-reloads template changes — essential for visual iteration
Export PreviewProps from each template for the preview server: export const PreviewProps: OTPEmailProps = { code: '847291', userName: 'Ray' }
Preview server is dev-only; never deployed to production

layer_2_token_security.description: Cryptographic OTP and magic link token generation and verification

truths: Generate 6-digit OTP: const bytes = crypto.randomBytes(4); const otp = (bytes.readUInt32BE(0) % 1000000).toString().padStart(6, '0')
This uses CSPRNG — never use Math.floor(Math.random() * 1000000)
6 digits = 1,000,000 possibilities; with 10-minute TTL and rate limiting, brute force is infeasible
Store HMAC of the OTP, not the raw OTP: crypto.createHmac('sha256', HMAC_SECRET).update(otp).digest('hex')
HMAC_SECRET is a server-only env var (min 32 bytes entropy); never NEXT_PUBLIC_
Comparison: regenerate HMAC from user input, compare with crypto.timingSafeEqual(Buffer.from(stored), Buffer.from(computed))
timingSafeEqual prevents timing attacks where attacker deduces correctness by measuring response time
Generate 256-bit (32-byte) opaque token: const token = crypto.randomBytes(32).toString('hex') — 64 hex chars
This is the lookup key stored in DB and sent in URL — it IS the credential
Optionally HMAC-sign the (email, token) tuple for double verification: const sig = hmac(HMAC_SECRET, email + ':' + token)
URL: /auth/verify?token={token}&sig={sig} — verify sig server-side before DB lookup
Store SHA-256 hash of the token in DB, not the raw token: crypto.createHash('sha256').update(token).digest('hex')
On verification: hash the incoming token, look up the hash in DB — raw token never stored at rest
256-bit entropy with 15-minute TTL makes brute force statistically impossible (2^256 search space)
Use a single atomic UPDATE to consume: UPDATE email_login_tokens SET used_at = NOW() WHERE token_hash = $1 AND used_at IS NULL AND expires_at > NOW() AND email = $2 RETURNING user_id, id
If RETURNING returns no rows: token is expired, already used, or invalid — return generic 'invalid or expired link' error
Never reveal whether token was used vs expired vs not found — prevents oracle attacks
Do NOT use SELECT then UPDATE — race condition allows token reuse under concurrent requests
After consuming token: create authenticated session (httpOnly cookie, iron-session, or auth library token)
Delete or retain consumed tokens based on audit policy; if retaining: DELETE WHERE used_at < NOW() - INTERVAL '24 hours' in cleanup job
Rate limit token requests by email address: max 3 requests per 15 minutes per email
Rate limit token verification attempts by IP: max 5 failed attempts per 15 minutes per IP
Implement in PostgreSQL: count rows WHERE email = $1 AND created_at > NOW() - INTERVAL '15 minutes' before inserting new token
Return HTTP 429 (or Server Action error state) with 'Too many requests' — do not reveal count
For OTP: invalidate all previous unused tokens for that email before generating a new one (prevents code accumulation)
For magic link: same — DELETE WHERE email = $1 AND used_at IS NULL AND expires_at > NOW() before inserting fresh token
Consider Upstash Redis for distributed rate limiting if running multiple Next.js pods; postgres-based rate limit is adequate for moderate traffic
OTP code: user stays in the app tab — best UX for mobile/desktop flows where email app is separate; slightly lower security surface (manually typed = typo-proof by UX, not by crypto)
Magic link: one-click from email — most frictionless; risks email prefetching scanners auto-clicking the link (see: anti-scanning measures)
Anti-scanner for magic link: use POST confirmation page — link leads to /auth/confirm page that shows a 'Complete login' button; actual token consumption on POST, not GET
Offer both flows in one UI: 'Enter the 6-digit code OR click the link in your email'
Magic link prefetch protection: check User-Agent for known scanner bots before consuming; or require explicit POST confirmation
OTP brute force: 1M possibilities / 3 attempts per 15 min window = ~1.4 billion years to exhaust

layer_3_postgres_schema.description: PostgreSQL 15 DDL and queries for email login tokens

truths: Table name: email_login_tokens — dedicated table; not a column on users
Supports both OTP and magic link flows in same table via flow_type ENUM
token_hash stores SHA-256 hex of raw token (magic link) or HMAC-SHA-256 of OTP — never raw token
email column: VARCHAR(254) NOT NULL — max RFC-5321 email length; indexed for rate-limit queries
expires_at: TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL — set at insertion; 10 min for OTP, 15 min for magic link
used_at: TIMESTAMPTZ NULL — NULL = unused; set atomically on consumption
user_id: UUID NULL REFERENCES users(id) ON DELETE CASCADE — NULL before user exists (registration flow), set for returning user flow
ip_address: INET NULL — requester IP for audit and rate limiting
attempt_count: SMALLINT NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 — incremented on each failed OTP verification attempt; lock at threshold
CREATE TYPE email_flow_type AS ENUM ('otp_code', 'magic_link');

CREATE TABLE email_login_tokens (id UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(), email VARCHAR(254) NOT NULL, token_hash VARCHAR(64) NOT NULL, flow_type email_flow_type NOT NULL DEFAULT 'otp_code', user_id UUID REFERENCES users(id) ON DELETE CASCADE, expires_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL, used_at TIMESTAMPTZ, ip_address INET, attempt_count SMALLINT NOT NULL DEFAULT 0, created_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW());
UNIQUE(token_hash) — prevents accidental duplicate token storage (astronomically unlikely but enforced)
INDEX ON (email, created_at DESC) WHERE used_at IS NULL — supports rate limit count query
INDEX ON (token_hash) WHERE used_at IS NULL — atomic consumption lookup
INDEX ON (expires_at) WHERE used_at IS NULL — cleanup cron target
RLS: ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY; policy allows only app_readwrite role for INSERT/UPDATE; login_verifier role SELECT + UPDATE(used_at, attempt_count) only
Rate limit check: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM email_login_tokens WHERE email = $1 AND created_at > NOW() - INTERVAL '15 minutes'
Invalidate old unused tokens: DELETE FROM email_login_tokens WHERE email = $1 AND used_at IS NULL AND expires_at > NOW()
Insert new token: INSERT INTO email_login_tokens (email, token_hash, flow_type, user_id, expires_at, ip_address) VALUES ($1, $2, $3, $4, NOW() + $5::INTERVAL, $6) RETURNING id
Atomic consumption: UPDATE email_login_tokens SET used_at = NOW() WHERE token_hash = $1 AND email = $2 AND used_at IS NULL AND expires_at > NOW() RETURNING user_id, id
Increment attempt: UPDATE email_login_tokens SET attempt_count = attempt_count + 1 WHERE token_hash = $1 AND used_at IS NULL RETURNING attempt_count
Cleanup cron: DELETE FROM email_login_tokens WHERE expires_at < NOW() - INTERVAL '24 hours'
email_login_tokens lives in the application database — same CloudNativePG cluster as users table
Separate DB role 'login_verifier': GRANT SELECT, UPDATE (used_at, attempt_count) ON email_login_tokens TO login_verifier — Server Action for verification uses this role
App_readwrite role: GRANT INSERT, DELETE ON email_login_tokens TO app_readwrite — for token creation and cleanup
RLS policy: app_readwrite role bypasses RLS with BYPASSRLS; login_verifier applies RLS WHERE email = current_setting('app.current_email')::TEXT if needed
WAL archiving covers this table automatically — no special backup config
Partition by created_at (monthly) if >1M tokens/month expected for efficient cleanup

layer_4_nextjs16_flow.description: Next.js 16 App Router implementation of the two-step passwordless login

truths: Step 1 — Request: user enters email → Server Action requestLoginCode() → generates token → sends email → returns { step: 'verify', maskedEmail }
Step 2 — Verify (OTP): user enters 6-digit code → Server Action verifyLoginCode() → validates → creates session → redirect('/dashboard')
Step 2 — Verify (magic link): user clicks link in email → GET /auth/verify → confirmation page → POST Server Action consumeMagicLink() → create session → redirect
Both steps handled by useActionState in a single 'use client' login page component
State machine: { step: 'email' | 'verify' | 'success', error?, maskedEmail? } — drives UI branch rendering
Progressive enhancement: form with <form action={serverAction}> works without JS; useActionState adds pending states on top
'use server' at top of actions file
requestLoginCode(prevState, formData): validate email with Zod (z.string().email()); normalize to lowercase and trim
Check rate limit in DB (max 3 requests per 15 min per email); if exceeded return { error: 'Too many requests. Try again later.' }
Invalidate previous unused tokens for this email (DELETE WHERE email = $1 AND used_at IS NULL)
Generate OTP or magic link token using crypto.randomBytes()
Hash token: HMAC for OTP, SHA-256 for magic link token
Insert into email_login_tokens with appropriate expires_at interval
Render email template: const html = await render(<OTPEmail code={otp} />); const text = await render(<OTPEmail code={otp} />, { plainText: true })
Send via transporter.sendMail({ from, to: email, subject, html, text })
Return { step: 'verify', maskedEmail: maskEmail(email), flowType: 'otp_code' } — never return the token or OTP to client
verifyLoginCode(prevState, formData): extract email (from hidden input, never trust client for user_id) and otp from formData
Validate otp: Zod z.string().length(6).regex(/^\d{6}$/)
Compute HMAC of submitted OTP: crypto.createHmac('sha256', HMAC_SECRET).update(otp).digest('hex')
Fetch token row: SELECT id, token_hash, attempt_count, user_id FROM email_login_tokens WHERE email = $1 AND used_at IS NULL AND expires_at > NOW()
If no row: return { error: 'Code expired or invalid' }
If attempt_count >= 5: return { error: 'Too many failed attempts. Request a new code.' }
Compare HMACs with crypto.timingSafeEqual() — constant time
On mismatch: increment attempt_count; return { error: 'Invalid code' }
On match: atomic UPDATE SET used_at = NOW() WHERE id = $1 RETURNING user_id
Create session (httpOnly cookie); redirect('/dashboard')
Route: app/auth/verify/page.tsx — Server Component that reads searchParams.token and searchParams.email
Do NOT consume token on GET — show a confirmation page with a form containing a hidden token field
Confirmation page renders: 'Click below to complete your login' + <form action={consumeMagicLink}><button>Log in</button></form>
This pattern defeats email prefetch scanners that auto-GET URLs in emails
consumeMagicLink(prevState, formData) Server Action: extract token from hidden input
Hash token: crypto.createHash('sha256').update(token).digest('hex')
Atomic UPDATE consumption query; on success create session and redirect
Import: import { useActionState } from 'react' — NOT from 'react-dom' (React 19)
useFormState is deprecated in React 19 / Next.js 16 — use useActionState exclusively
Signature: const [state, formAction, isPending] = useActionState(serverAction, initialState)
initialState: { step: 'email', error: null, maskedEmail: null }
Server Action signature: async function action(prevState: State, formData: FormData): Promise<State>
Render branch: if (state.step === 'verify') render OTP input form; else render email input form
isPending: disable submit button and show loading spinner while action is in-flight
Pass maskedEmail as hidden input in verify step — do not re-ask user for email
LoginPage: 'use client'; renders two-step UI based on state.step
Step 1 form: email input + submit → calls requestLoginCode action
Step 2 form (OTP): hidden email input + 6-box OTP input + submit → calls verifyLoginCode action
OTP input UX: 6 separate single-character <input type='text' maxLength={1}> auto-advancing on input; or single <input type='text' inputMode='numeric' pattern='[0-9]*' maxLength={6}>
Single wide OTP input is simpler and more accessible — recommended over 6-box approach
After paste: strip non-numeric chars and fill the input; JavaScript paste handler recommended

Error display: {state.error &&

{state.error}

}
Resend code button: calls requestLoginCode again with same email (hidden in form)

layer_5_email_deliverability.description: Making sure self-hosted email reaches the inbox, not spam

truths: PTR record: IP → mail.yourdomain.com (reverse DNS — set via hosting provider / ISP)
A record: mail.yourdomain.com → your IP
MX record: not strictly required for outbound-only sender but recommended
SPF: 'v=spf1 ip4:YOUR_IP -all' on the sending domain
DKIM: generate 2048-bit RSA key pair; publish public key as TXT record at <selector>._domainkey.<domain>
DMARC: 'v=DMARC1; p=quarantine; rua=mailto:dmarc@domain; pct=100'
All four (PTR+SPF+DKIM+DMARC) are required for reliable inbox delivery in 2025 — any missing one degrades deliverability significantly
Configure DKIM in Nodemailer transporter: dkim: { domainName: 'yourdomain.com', keySelector: 'login2025', privateKey: process.env.DKIM_PRIVATE_KEY }
DKIM_PRIVATE_KEY: server-only env var; PEM-encoded RSA private key; never NEXT_PUBLIC_
Nodemailer signs each message automatically with the DKIM config on the transporter
Use a dedicated key selector for transactional login emails (separate from newsletter selector) for independent rotation
Subject lines for OTP: 'Your login code: {code}' — clear, expected, not spammy
Subject lines for magic link: 'Your login link for {AppName}' — specific and branded
Never ALL CAPS subject lines
Include physical mailing address in footer (CAN-SPAM requirement for US; GDPR best practice globally)
Unsubscribe link not required for transactional authentication emails but include a 'help' link
Text:HTML ratio — react-email plain-text rendering ensures good ratio automatically
Avoid spam trigger words in OTP emails: 'free', 'click here', 'confirm your account' (prefer 'complete your login')
New IP: warm up by sending to engaged users first; don't blast 10K emails on day 1
Bounce handling: implement a webhook or IMAP listener to mark hard-bounced emails; stop sending to them
Unsubscribe/block list: maintain in DB; check before sending any email (including transactional)
Monitor blacklists: MXToolbox, Spamhaus — check weekly when starting out
Dedicated IP for transactional vs. dedicated IP for marketing if volume warrants it

layer_6_security_hardening.description: Security model for the full email login system

truths: SMTP_HOST, SMTP_PORT, SMTP_USER, SMTP_PASS — server-only; never NEXT_PUBLIC_
OTP_HMAC_SECRET — min 32 bytes random hex; used to HMAC OTPs before storage
DKIM_PRIVATE_KEY — PEM RSA private key for DKIM signing
EMAIL_FROM — 'AppName <noreply@auth.yourdomain.com>'
Store all in K8s Secrets (or .env.local for development only; never commit to Git)
Rotate OTP_HMAC_SECRET annually; all active tokens (already short-lived) will be invalidated on rotation — acceptable
After successful token consumption: create server-side session — httpOnly, Secure, SameSite=Lax cookie
Use iron-session, Auth.js v5 JWT, or custom PASETO token — not localStorage
Session must encode user_id, issued_at, expires_at — validate on every request in middleware
Rotate session ID/token on login to prevent session fixation attacks
Set short initial session (e.g., 7 days) with sliding window renewal on activity
Server Actions in Next.js 16 include built-in CSRF protection via origin check for same-origin form submissions
For extra hardness: validate Referer/Origin header in Server Action if called from sensitive operations
SameSite=Lax on session cookie prevents most CSRF scenarios for navigation-triggered forms
Magic link GET → POST confirmation pattern also functions as CSRF protection (attacker can GET the link but cannot POST the confirmation from another origin)
Never reveal whether an email address exists in the system — always return 'If this email is registered, a code was sent' (prevents email enumeration)
For token errors: always use generic 'Invalid or expired code/link' — never 'Token not found' vs 'Token expired' (oracle)
For rate limit: 'Too many requests. Please wait before trying again.' — don't reveal count or window duration
Log detailed errors server-side (with correlation ID) but return only safe messages to client

layer_7_common_pitfalls.description: Real failure modes in email login systems

truth_lens.problem: Build fails with 'renderAsync is not a function' after upgrading react-email
truth_lens.cause: react-email 5 removes renderAsync; it was deprecated in v3
truth_lens.fix: Replace all renderAsync() with await render() — render() is now async by default in @react-email/render 2.x

truth_lens.problem: SMTP connection errors or extreme latency under load
truth_lens.cause: Creating a new nodemailer.createTransport() on every Server Action invocation — opens new TLS handshake each time
truth_lens.fix: Module-level singleton transporter in lib/mailer.ts; use pool: true for own SMTP server

truth_lens.problem: Users report 'link already used' immediately after clicking
truth_lens.cause: Email security scanners (Barracuda, Proofpoint, Microsoft SafeLinks) auto-GET every URL in incoming emails
truth_lens.fix: Never consume token on GET; use POST confirmation page pattern — scanner cannot POST

truth_lens.problem: Attacker can deduce correct OTP digits by measuring response time variance
truth_lens.cause: String comparison: if (storedHmac === computedHmac) — JavaScript string comparison short-circuits on first mismatch
truth_lens.fix: crypto.timingSafeEqual(Buffer.from(stored, 'hex'), Buffer.from(computed, 'hex')) — constant time regardless of match position

truth_lens.problem: Database breach exposes raw OTPs or magic link tokens — immediate account takeover for all valid tokens
truth_lens.cause: Storing raw OTP or raw magic link token in token column
truth_lens.fix: Store HMAC(OTP) for codes; store SHA-256(token) for magic links. Raw token is never persisted.

truth_lens.problem: Emails rejected by strict spam filters or unreadable in plain-text email clients
truth_lens.cause: Only setting html field in sendMail options; no text field
truth_lens.fix: Always render both: await render(component) for html; await render(component, { plainText: true }) for text; set both on sendMail

truth_lens.problem: React 19 / Next.js 16 build warning or runtime error on useFormState import
truth_lens.fix: Replace with useActionState from 'react'; update Server Action signature to include prevState as first param

truth_lens.problem: Attacker can determine which email addresses are registered by checking response messages
truth_lens.cause: Returning 'Email not found' vs 'Code sent' based on DB lookup result
truth_lens.fix: Always return the same response ('If this email is registered, a code was sent') regardless of whether email exists in users table

truth_lens.problem: Next.js crashes on render with 'Cannot use import statement in module' or similar
truth_lens.cause: react-email packages not in serverComponentsExternalPackages in next.config.ts

truth_lens.problem: Attacker floods system with OTP requests for a target email, causing email spam to the victim
truth_lens.cause: No rate limiting on token request endpoint
truth_lens.fix: Max 3 requests per 15 minutes per email address enforced at DB level before transporter.sendMail() is called

postgresql_schema.description: Complete production DDL for email_login_tokens — PostgreSQL 15 / CloudNativePG
ddl_sequence: CREATE TYPE email_flow_type AS ENUM ('otp_code', 'magic_link');
CREATE TABLE email_login_tokens (
id             UUID          PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
email          VARCHAR(254)  NOT NULL,
token_hash     VARCHAR(64)   NOT NULL,
flow_type      email_flow_type NOT NULL DEFAULT 'otp_code',
user_id        UUID          REFERENCES users(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
expires_at     TIMESTAMPTZ   NOT NULL,
used_at        TIMESTAMPTZ,
ip_address     INET,
attempt_count  SMALLINT      NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
created_at     TIMESTAMPTZ   NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW()
CREATE UNIQUE INDEX email_login_tokens_hash_uidx ON email_login_tokens (token_hash);
CREATE INDEX email_login_tokens_email_rate_idx ON email_login_tokens (email, created_at DESC) WHERE used_at IS NULL;
CREATE INDEX email_login_tokens_cleanup_idx ON email_login_tokens (expires_at) WHERE used_at IS NULL;
ALTER TABLE email_login_tokens ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY;
-- App write role: create and delete tokens
GRANT INSERT, DELETE ON email_login_tokens TO app_readwrite;
-- Login verifier role: read and consume tokens only
GRANT SELECT ON email_login_tokens TO login_verifier;
GRANT UPDATE (used_at, attempt_count) ON email_login_tokens TO login_verifier;
postgresql_schema.rate_limit_query: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM email_login_tokens WHERE email = $1 AND created_at > NOW() - INTERVAL '15 minutes'
postgresql_schema.invalidate_old_query: DELETE FROM email_login_tokens WHERE email = $1 AND used_at IS NULL AND flow_type = $2
postgresql_schema.insert_query: INSERT INTO email_login_tokens (email, token_hash, flow_type, user_id, expires_at, ip_address) VALUES ($1, $2, $3, $4, NOW() + $5::INTERVAL, $6) RETURNING id
postgresql_schema.atomic_consume_query: UPDATE email_login_tokens SET used_at = NOW() WHERE token_hash = $1 AND email = $2 AND used_at IS NULL AND expires_at > NOW() RETURNING user_id, id
postgresql_schema.increment_attempt_query: UPDATE email_login_tokens SET attempt_count = attempt_count + 1 WHERE id = $1 RETURNING attempt_count
postgresql_schema.cleanup_cron: DELETE FROM email_login_tokens WHERE expires_at < NOW() - INTERVAL '24 hours'

file_structure.description: Canonical file layout for the email login system in Next.js 16 App Router

files.note: pool: true for own SMTP; Ethereal fallback in dev; call verify() at startup
Props: { code, userName, appName, expiresInMinutes }; export PreviewProps for dev server

files.role: Login page — 'use client'; useActionState state machine
files.note: Renders email step or OTP verify step based on state.step

files.note: Reads searchParams.token; renders POST form; does NOT consume on GET

server_only: SMTP_HOST — hostname of own SMTP server
DKIM_PRIVATE_KEY — PEM RSA private key for DKIM signing
OTP_HMAC_SECRET — min 32-byte hex string for HMAC of OTP codes
dev_only: ETHEREAL_USER — Ethereal test account user (auto-created via createTestAccount())
EMAIL_MODE=ethereal — switches transporter to Ethereal in dev

anti_patterns: Storing raw OTP or raw magic link token in the database — DB breach = immediate account takeover for all valid tokens
String equality (===) for OTP comparison — timing side-channel; always use crypto.timingSafeEqual()
Creating new nodemailer.createTransport() inside the Server Action body — opens TLS handshake per email
Consuming magic link token on HTTP GET — email scanner bots auto-GET all URLs, instantly invalidating links
Using renderAsync() from @react-email/render — deprecated in v3, removed in v5; use await render()
Sending HTML-only email — no text field degrades deliverability and breaks plain-text email clients
Returning 'Email not found' vs 'Code sent' — email enumeration oracle; always return same message
Not rate-limiting token requests — attacker can spam victim's inbox with OTP emails
Not rate-limiting verification attempts — allows brute force of 6-digit OTP (1M attempts needed but no limit = feasible)
Using useFormState from 'react-dom' — deprecated in React 19; import useActionState from 'react'
Exposing SMTP credentials as NEXT_PUBLIC_ env vars — accessible to any browser that loads the page
Not adding react-email packages to serverComponentsExternalPackages in next.config.ts — causes SSR module resolution errors
SELECT then UPDATE for token consumption — race condition allows replay attack under concurrent requests; use single atomic UPDATE
Skipping SPF/DKIM/DMARC DNS records — emails immediately land in spam or are rejected by modern MTAs
Not sending plain-text version alongside HTML — CAN-SPAM requirement and deliverability best practice
